points.description: First valid reason stated precisely with correct technical terms. Accepted reasons: (a) ionisation of active sites/surface groups such as OH and COOH, dependent on pH of the medium; (b) imperfection in crystal structure (isomorphous replacement), e.g. atoms of low valency replacing silicon, reducing positive charge so net charge is negative; (c) adsorption of anions onto the particle surface.
points.partial_credit: Half only if the reason is clearly identified but a key part is missing (e.g. ionisation of OH/COOH groups without mention of pH, or crystal imperfection without the low-valency replacement idea).

points.description: Second, different valid reason from the same accepted list, stated precisely with correct technical terms. Must not repeat the first reason.
points.partial_credit: Half only if the reason is clearly identified but a key part is missing (as for P1).

rubric.notes: Full marks need two different reasons from the model answer (ionisation of active sites like OH/COOH depending on pH; crystal imperfection with low-valency atoms replacing silicon; adsorption of anions), each stated precisely with the correct terms. Part marks only where a reason is clearly identified but a key detail is missing. Vague answers such as "charge on surface" or "due to ions", or a wrong statement within a reason, earn nothing for that point; a repeated reason is credited once.
